public_rationale: Surge's November 18, 2026 benchmark documents errors in investment calculations and sentencing analysis across realistic legal assignments [e1]. Arca's evaluation, completed November 4 using runs from September through November, reports that its best system met every rubric requirement on 16 of 55 regulatory-affairs tasks [e2]. These findings support reliability concerns across multiple substantial professional applications where errors can have consequential effects [e1, e2].
limitations: The benchmarks do not establish reliability across all applications or every supervised or specialized deployment.
The documented benchmark errors do not establish that actual clients suffered harm.
Arca evaluates its own product alongside other systems, and its results do not isolate November performance [e2].
Failure to meet every rubric requirement does not establish that an answer provides no useful assistance.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current AI is still not trustworthy enough for many applications.

statement.excerpt: Clinging to the Riemann results like a life raft after the stock market correction– as AI hypesters on social media are doing—doesn’t change the fact that (a) current AI still isn’t trustworthy enough to for many applications and (b) is still not profitable enough to warrant the massive investments.
statement.document_title: Levent Alpöge has solved the Riemann Hypothesis with the help of Claude! What does it mean?

our_interpretation: Assess only the supplied normalized reliability claim, not the separate profitability assertion in the same sentence.
The plain reading is that current general-purpose AI cannot reliably complete many consequential applications without additional checking or safeguards.
'Many' means multiple substantial application classes, not every application or a majority of all possible uses.
For the ongoing state, use November 2026 through the day before publication, the current technical reporting window.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations show persistent consequential errors or frequent failures against professional requirements across multiple substantial application classes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations establish reliable completion at the required standard across those applications, including realistic inputs and deployment conditions.
